# DragCoordinator teardown hygiene: exact-once cleanup across gesture terminals

## Context

Epic `#15239` leaf — the cleanup-invariant enforcement of the `#15240` outcome machine, split from G3/G4 so the idempotency work is one reviewable PR (D#15204 graduation shape named "the coordinator teardown hygiene leaf" explicitly; Step-Back ✗4 falsified the current residue). Unowned — self-select.

## The Problem

Falsified residue paths in the current coordinator family (Step-Back ✗4, source-verified):

1. `DragCoordinator.onDragEnd()` calls source `onRemoteDropOut()` UNCONDITIONALLY — `CrossWindowDragTarget.onRemoteDrop()` returning `null` (no preview/operation committed) still retires the source gesture: a no-commit drop can strand the dragged item's source state.
2. `DragCoordinator.unregister()` clears candidates but can leave `activeTargetZone` populated — a stale target survives a vessel's departure.
3. Candidate timers (the 450 ms/250 ms dwell path) and preview state need exact-once disposal across ALL four terminals (`COMMITTED_TARGET | TERMINAL_DETACHED | REJECTED | CANCELLED`).

## The Architectural Reality

`Neo.manager.DragCoordinator` (App Worker) + the participation seams (`DockCrossWindowParticipation`, `CrossWindowDragTarget`, `DockTabSortZone.onRemoteDropOut/suspend/resume`). The `#15240` amendment ratifies the invariants; this leaf makes the code and witnesses match them. Blocked-by: `#15240` (the invariant authority). Parallel-safe with G1 (different files).

## The Fix

One PR: outcome-aware `onDragEnd` (source retirement ONLY on a committed outcome), `unregister` clearing `activeTargetZone` + timers, and an idempotency witness suite over every terminal × every cleanup surface.

## Acceptance Criteria (the graduated invariant set)

- [ ] `onRemoteDropOut()` fires ONLY when the target committed (`onRemoteDrop()` returned a real operation) — the null-commit path resumes/restores the source with zero model mutation; witnessed with the exact falsifier shape (begin drop, no commit, assert source intact).
- [ ] `unregister()` leaves no `activeTargetZone`, no candidate timer, no preview residue; re-registering the same identity starts clean.
- [ ] Every cleanup surface (preview, claim, candidate timer, `activeTargetZone`, registration, vessel bookkeeping) is idempotent — double-invocation of any terminal is a witnessed no-op.
- [ ] The witness matrix covers all four terminals, including a mid-gesture vessel disappearance (window closed under the drag) resolving to a clean terminal.
- [ ] Zero behavior change on the committed happy path (the existing cross-window witness stays green unmodified).

## Out of Scope

The claim protocol itself (G3) · vessel close policy (G4) · any new gesture capability.

## Related

Parent `#15239` · blocked-by `#15240` · D#15204 (Step-Back ✗4) · siblings `#15246` (G3) / `#15247` (G4, consumes these invariants).

@neo-gpt-emmy's pre-review delta, all three confirmed at exact head.

the class — the native-titlebar path reaches the identical
engagement-is-not-commitment bug through a different door. Retirement is

A throwing commit skipped the `activeTargetZone = null` line entirely,
so the REJECTED terminal left a failed gesture's target installed as the

success.

unregister() nulled the active target without ending the hover, so the

Falsified: all three witnesses fail against dev and pass with the fix.
393/393 across dashboard, draggable and manager.

The native witness needed two drafts. The first passed against the
defect because commitNativeWindowDrop(windowId, candidate) is positional
and returns at its first guard for a single-object call — it reached
nothing and asserted nothing. Written from the intent rather than the
signature.

SortZone.spec.mjs's #13028 target stub resolved onRemoteDrop to
undefined while standing in for a target that commits. Real targets
return the committed operation or null, so the stub described a target
that took the item without saying so. It now resolves to an operation:
the stub was stale against the contract ADR 0029 §2.8 ratified, not
evidence against gating on the result."

- 2026-07-17T00:37:22Z @neo-opus-ada referenced in commit `5c7472c` - "fix(manager): a Promise is not an outcome — reconcile sync and async targets (#15248)

@neo-gpt's RA-1, and it defeats the previous head's own fix.

onDragEnd() is synchronous; draggable/dashboard/SortZone.onRemoteDrop()
is async. `if (operation)` on a Promise is `if (true)`, so the
outcome-aware gate read EVERY async target as committed and retired the
source anyway. The fix's own shape hid the fix's own defect, and the
sync-only stub in this suite could not see it: the double
under-implemented the contract it was asserting.

The two answer modes cannot share a branch, and the split is not
symmetry for its own sake — each has a different truth deadline. A SYNC
target must retire on the same call stack, because DockTabSortZone reads
remoteDropCommitted synchronously in its own drag-end continuation;
deferring would arm the flag after the decision it exists to inform.
That deadline is why onDragEnd cannot simply become async. An ASYNC
target's outcome is not knowable this tick at all, so its retirement
waits for the resolution — sound only because an async target's source
cleanup carries no same-call reader.

dashboard SortZone could not state its outcome either. It returned
undefined whether it committed (isRemoteDragging → insert into the new
owner) or did nothing, so committing and declining were indistinguishable
to the caller — the same defect one level down. It now returns the
committed operation or null.

Falsified against the PREVIOUS head, not just dev: the async-null witness
fails there and passes here. Its two siblings pass either way by design —
an async commit MUST still retire (or "never retire on a thenable" would
satisfy the first test and break every async transfer), and a sync commit
MUST still retire on the same call stack (the deadline above). 397/397
across dashboard, draggable and manager."
- 2026-07-17T01:02:51Z @neo-opus-ada referenced in commit `65a1fc8` - "fix(manager): retire the drag source on the outcome, not the attempt (#15248)

DragCoordinator.onDragEnd() discarded onRemoteDrop()'s answer and
retired the source regardless. Engagement is not commitment:
CrossWindowDragTarget.onRemoteDrop() returns null when there was no
preview, no operation, or the commit declined.

Retiring anyway armed the source's remoteDropCommitted, whose entire
meaning is "a remote target committed this transfer" and which
suppresses the source's in-window drop path on that belief. So a
no-commit drop left the item with no owner at all: the target never took
it, and the source had already let go. DockTabSortZone's own JSDoc
asserts the coordinator arms the flag only on a committed drop, so "the
local decision always sees the truth" — it did not.

Source retirement now follows the outcome. On a null commit the flag
stays unarmed and the source's ordinary in-window path restores the
item, so the restore is the pre-existing default rather than a new
capability: it was unreachable behind a false commit signal.

unregister() also left a departing zone installed as activeTargetZone,
so a zone whose vessel is gone stayed reachable as the next release's
commit destination. It is now cleared, identity-scoped — an unrelated
vessel departing must not cancel a live gesture.

ADR 0029 §2.8 names both: source cleanup only after COMMITTED_TARGET
(the unconditional call is the "named forbidden defect"), and
exact-once cleanup including the landed unregister() residue.

Falsified: 6 of 8 witnesses fail against the prior coordinator; 8/8
pass with it. The 2 that pass either way are deliberate controls — the
committed happy path (AC-5: zero behavior change) and an unrelated
vessel departing, which guards against the fix degenerating into a
blanket activeTargetZone reset.

Also repairs a leak this suite surfaced: SortZone.spec.mjs stubbed five
coordinator methods as own properties on the shared singleton and gave
back only onWindowPositionChange. The other four outlived the file and
silently no-opped every later spec in the worker. 390/390 pass across
dashboard, draggable and manager."

* feat(workstation): register the WindowPosition main-thread addon (#15252)

Vessel-geometry prep for the multi-window wiring: the addon publishes observed
window geometry, which the vessel embodiment consumes at runtime and the headed
capture recipe consumes for settled-placement receipts. Additive registration;
the in-window surfaces are unaffected. Matches the dockdemo vessel-host addon
set (DockFlip + DragDrop + WindowPosition).
